current.text: Verify that HTTP responses include a Content-Security-Policy response header field which defines directives to ensure the browser only loads and executes trusted content or resources, in order to limit execution of malicious JavaScript. As a minimum, a global policy must be used which includes the directives object-src 'none' and base-uri 'none' and defines either an allowlist or uses nonces or hashes. For an L3 application, a per-response policy with nonces or hashes must be defined.

summaries.body:
The 5.0.0 mapping records V3.4.3 as MODIFIED, moved from 4.0.3 V14.4.3, which required a CSP response header to help mitigate XSS (HTML, DOM, JSON, and JavaScript injection). The current clause still requires CSP, but specifies minimum directives (object-src 'none', base-uri 'none', plus an allowlist or nonces/hashes) and, at L3, a per-response policy with nonces or hashes.

The mapping notes that predecessor text is dissimilar and that git/content lineage diverges from the ID slot. Predecessor-ID events include tghosth's 16 May 2019 resolve of #643 and 2 June 2020 header-wording clarification (#793). Commits stamped V3.4.3 are old session-management occupancy. Mapping and the V14.4.3 predecessor text are the reliable origin.

The attested 5.0 change is from a general CSP-mitigates-XSS sentence to named minimum directives and an L3 per-response nonce/hash policy. #643 and #793 are 4.0-era header wording on V14.4.3, not that directive list. Issue #478 (splitting V14.4 subcategories) is chapter structure around the predecessor.

Session-management CWEs, spacing tweaks, URL fixes, and capitalisation commits on the V3.4.3 number did not rewrite this CSP control.
